To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of the BSI to assess the psychiatric status of rural community mental health clients is a useful tool for predicting their level of psychiatric symptoms 3 months later.

1) rural community mental health clients have a higher prevalence of psychiatric symptoms, 2) rural community mental
health clients with more psychiatric symptoms are more likely to be unemployed and to have lower incomes, 3) rural clients with more psychiatric symptomatology are more likely to report more negative service experiences, and 4) rural community mental clients with more psychiatric problems are more likely to have more negative perceptions of the services they received.

the BSI is a useful measure of psychiatric symptomatology in rural community mental health clients, and that a model of predicting change in psychiatric symptomatology over time includes client characteristics (income, age, and initial symptomatology) as well as the evaluation of the service provided.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model of the process of change in the mental health status of rural clients in community mental health programs.
identifying factors that predict psychiatric symptoms in rural community mental health clients.
the identification of variables which can be used to predict the presence or absence of psychiatric symptoms in a sample of rural clients in community mental health settings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BSI has not been adequately tested for the purpose of predicting psychiatric symptomatology in rural clients, and the results of the present study should be viewed with caution.
the BSI is a reliable and valid instrument that can be used in the rural mental health setting to measure the severity of psychiatric symptoms. (Author/BL)
the BSI is useful in predicting psychiatric symptoms in rural community mental health clients, and that this instrument is a useful adjunct to clinical practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated the feasibility of conducting research in rural areas, that we have developed an effective and efficient research design for rural community mental health clients, that our findings are consistent with those of other studies, that we have found a model of psychiatric symptoms that can be used to predict psychiatric symptoms, and that we have demonstrated that the model is useful for predicting symptoms 3 mo. after the initial evaluation.
the BSI has good psychometric properties and is useful in the assessment of psychiatric symptomatology.
the BSI is useful in predicting psychiatric status and that the BSI may be used as a screening instrument in the rural setting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to identify a set of variables that predict the severity of symptoms at 3 mo. after the first visit.
the Brief Symptom Index (BSI) is a useful and efficient instrument for measuring psychiatric symptoms in rural community mental health clients.
